scope: SC-09 writer-lock metadata, public diagnostics, isolated tests and recovery guide; read-only source review with isolated test execution.

checks.observation: Exclusive O_CREAT|O_EXCL acquisition and finally release remain. Initialize, commit, load, publication and atomic-write function ASTs match HEAD; CAS reload/hash/revision checks are unchanged.

At most 4097 bytes are read from a 4096-byte accepted record. Initial lstat rejects non-regular/oversized files; descriptor/path identity and before/after metadata checks discard detected changes. Read failures retain contention. O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK are used where available. This is not a malicious-filesystem guarantee.

New records add host and UTC acquisition time. Legacy PID-only JSON remains readable. PID is bounded and excludes booleans; optional host/time are bounded and validated. Duplicates, non-JSON constants, invalid UTF-8 and malformed/deep records do not expose payloads or grant recovery authority.

No PID liveness query, automatic age-based deletion, wait loop or retry was added. Existing locks stay in place on refusal, including old, malformed and unreadable records. A lock disappearing during observation is reported changed and is not reacquired by that call.

store_locked preserves error/detail and adds the existing unfinished_work category with inspect_lock_owner. The optional lock field copies only runtime error context and whitelisted fields; request arguments cannot invent observed owner data. CLI and MCP diagnostics agree. CLI exits 2; MCP returns isError in its successful transport process.

The exact lock path is surfaced without manufacturing a state.px read beneath PLAR/handoff lock folders. Recovery directs the caller to reconcile the affected store, PLAR or handoff and preserves unknown remote attempts.

Path and descriptor ctime are compared within the same stat API; existing directory PermissionError becomes non_regular contention, while permission failure with no observed lock remains the original access failure. Both regressions are covered by passing tests.

Guide requires establishing quiescence for all writers, preserving exact leftover bytes and owning-session evidence, then explicit movement to a fresh location. It explains successor-lock cleanup risk and does not claim atomic compare-and-unlink. The additive local lock metadata does not change saved PX1/PX2 document/registry semantics or require a migration.

limits: This review does not establish native model instruction following, artistic quality, real PixelLab execution, engine acceptance or human acceptance.
The Windows symlink test was skipped for privilege; non-regular handling was source-reviewed and directory behavior was executed.
Metadata is best-effort advisory observation, not proof of process liveness, distributed exclusion or protection from a malicious filesystem writer.
The reviewer did not run the full verification suite, rebuild generated bundles, or independently execute the parent process-crash recovery proof.
Source AST comparison establishes unchanged commit/publication code; broader concurrency/process evidence belongs to separately retained root verification.
M1/M2 and broader M3/M4/M5 remain open; human acceptance remains separate.
